steps.message:
I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Today is Saturday, October 24, 2026. Submissions close six days from today, on Friday, at 11:59 PM PT."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

I need to find the deadline in Madrid time.

Given information:
- Today is Saturday, October 24, 2026
- Deadline is 6 days from today = Friday, October 30, 2026
- Time: 11:59 PM PT (Pacific Time)

In late October, both Pacific Time and Madrid time will be observing daylight saving time:
- PT (Pacific Daylight Time/PDT) is UTC-7
- Madrid (Central European Summer Time/CEST) is UTC+2

Wait, let me check the DST dates for 2026:
- In the US, DST ends on the first Sunday of November (November 1, 2026)
- In the EU, DST ends on the last Sunday of October (October 25, 2026)

So on October 30, 2026:
- Pacific Time will still be in PDT (UTC-7) since DST doesn't end until November 1
- Madrid will be in CET (UTC+1) since DST ended on October 25

Time difference: Madrid is 8 hours ahead of Pacific Time on this date.

11:59 PM PT on October 30, 2026 = 23:59 October 30 PT
Adding 8 hours: 23:59 + 8:00 = 7:59 AM on October 31, 2026

ANSWER: 2026-10-31 07:59

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Today is Friday, October 30, 2026. The form closes this coming Monday at 10:00 AM Los Angeles time."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

I need to find when Monday, November 2, 2026 at 10:00 AM Los Angeles time is in Madrid time.

**Time zone information:**
- Los Angeles is in the Pacific Time Zone
- In late October/early November 2026, Los Angeles will be in PDT (Pacific Daylight Time), which is UTC-7
- Actually, I need to check: Daylight Saving Time in the US typically ends on the first Sunday of November
- October 30, 2026 is a Friday, so "this coming Monday" is November 2, 2026
- DST in the US in 2026 would end on November 1, 2026 (first Sunday of November)
- So on November 2, Los Angeles will be in PST (Pacific Standard Time), which is UTC-8

- Madrid is in CET (Central European Time)
- In early November, Spain will be in CET (UTC+1) as their DST (CEST) typically ends in late October
- Spain's DST in 2026 would end on October 25, 2026 (last Sunday of October)
- So on November 2, Madrid will be in CET (UTC+1)

**Time conversion:**
- Los Angeles: November 2, 2026, 10:00 AM PST (UTC-8)
- Convert to UTC: 10:00 AM + 8 hours = 6:00 PM UTC (18:00 UTC) on November 2
- Convert to Madrid (UTC+1): 6:00 PM + 1 hour = 7:00 PM (19:00)

ANSWER: 2026-11-02 19:00

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "The hackathon starts Saturday, October 24, 2026 at 18:00 Madrid time and lasts exactly 48 hours."
When is the end of the hackathon in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

I need to find when the hackathon ends in Madrid time.

Starting time: Saturday, October 24, 2026 at 18:00 Madrid time
Duration: 48 hours

Adding 48 hours to the start time:
- From Saturday 18:00, adding 24 hours gets to Sunday, October 25, 2026 at 18:00
- Adding another 24 hours gets to Monday, October 26, 2026 at 18:00

Since you live in Madrid and the contest is also in Madrid time, no timezone conversion is needed.

ANSWER: 2026-10-26 18:00

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "The final round starts October 26, 2026 at 10:00 AM PT; submissions close exactly 72 hours later."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

I need to figure out when 72 hours after October 26, 2026 at 10:00 AM PT is, converted to Madrid time.

First, let me establish the time zones:
- PT = Pacific Time (US West Coast)
- Madrid is in CEST (Central European Summer Time) or CET (Central European Time)

On October 26, 2026:
- Pacific Time will be in PDT (Pacific Daylight Time, UTC-7) since the US changes clocks on November 1, 2026
- Madrid will be in CET (Central European Time, UTC+1) since Europe changes clocks on October 25, 2026

So the time difference is: Madrid is 8 hours ahead of Pacific Time.

Starting time: October 26, 2026 at 10:00 AM PT
In Madrid: October 26, 2026 at 18:00 (6:00 PM)

Deadline: 72 hours later
72 hours = 3 days

October 26 at 10:00 AM PT + 72 hours = October 29 at 10:00 AM PT

Converting to Madrid time: October 29, 2026 at 18:00

ANSWER: 2026-10-29 18:00

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Submissions close October 31, 2026 at 11:59 PM ET. Results are announced exactly 36 hours after submissions close."
When is the results announcement in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

I need to figure out when the results will be announced in Madrid time.

First, let me establish the timeline:
- Submissions close: October 31, 2026 at 11:59 PM ET
- Results announced: 36 hours after that

Step 1: Convert submission deadline from ET to UTC
October 31, 2026 at 11:59 PM ET
In late October, ET is EDT (Eastern Daylight Time), which is UTC-4.
So 11:59 PM ET = 3:59 AM UTC on November 1, 2026

Step 2: Add 36 hours to the deadline
November 1, 2026 at 3:59 AM UTC + 36 hours = November 2, 2026 at 3:59 PM UTC

Step 3: Convert from UTC to Madrid time
In early November, Madrid is on CET (Central European Time), which is UTC+1.
November 2, 2026 at 3:59 PM UTC = November 2, 2026 at 4:59 PM CET

ANSWER: 2026-11-02 16:59

I live in Tokyo, Japan. A contest page says: "Deadline (Unix timestamp, seconds): 1791788340."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

I need to convert the Unix timestamp 1791788340 to Tokyo local time.

Unix timestamp 1791788340 represents the number of seconds since January 1, 1970 00:00:00 UTC.

Let me convert this:
- 1791788340 seconds from Unix epoch
- This equals approximately 56.8 years from 1970
- 1970 + 56.8 ≈ 2026-2027

More precisely:
- 1791788340 seconds ÷ 86400 seconds/day = 20,738.8 days
- 20,738 days from January 1, 1970 = approximately October 11, 2026

Converting to exact date and time:
- Unix timestamp 1791788340 = October 11, 2026 at 11:59:00 UTC

Tokyo is in JST (Japan Standard Time), which is UTC+9.

Therefore: October 11, 2026 11:59:00 UTC + 9 hours = October 11, 2026 20:59:00 JST

ANSWER: 2026-10-11 20:59

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Deadline: 2026-10-25T02:30:00Z."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

I need to convert 2026-10-25T02:30:00Z to Madrid local time.

The "Z" indicates this is in UTC (Coordinated Universal Time).

Madrid, Spain is in the Central European Time zone:
- During winter (standard time): UTC+1
- During summer (daylight saving time): UTC+2

On October 25, 2026, I need to check if Spain is still observing daylight saving time. In Europe, daylight saving time typically ends on the last Sunday of October. 

Let me check: October 2026 starts on a Thursday (since I can calculate that October 25, 2026 is a Sunday - actually let me recalculate). October 25, 2026 would need to be checked, but the last Sunday of October 2026 would be October 25, 2026 itself.

In the EU, clocks go back at 01:00 UTC on the last Sunday of October (which is 03:00 local summer time becoming 02:00 local standard time).

So on October 25, 2026 at 02:30:00 UTC:
- This is after the daylight saving time has ended (which happens at 01:00 UTC)
- Therefore Madrid will be on standard time (UTC+1)
- 02:30 UTC + 1 hour = 03:30 local time

ANSWER: 2026-10-25 03:30

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Entries close at 11:59 PM Pacific Time on the last Sunday of October 2026."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

I need to find the last Sunday of October 2026 and convert 11:59 PM Pacific Time to Madrid time.

First, let me identify the last Sunday of October 2026:
- October 2026 ends on October 31st
- I need to figure out what day of the week that is and count back to the last Sunday
- October 31, 2026 is a Saturday
- So the last Sunday of October 2026 is October 25, 2026

Now for the time conversion from Pacific Time to Madrid time on October 25, 2026:
- In late October, the US will have ended Daylight Saving Time (it ends the first Sunday of November, which is November 1, 2026)
- Actually, wait - let me reconsider. In 2026, the first Sunday of November is November 1st, so DST ends on November 1, 2026
- On October 25, 2026, Pacific Time is still in PDT (Pacific Daylight Time = UTC-7)
- Spain will have already switched to standard time (CET = UTC+1) by late October, as Europe typically changes the last Sunday of October
- Wait, October 25 IS the last Sunday of October - this is the day Europe switches from CEST to CET
- The switch happens at 3:00 AM local time, so by 11:59 PM PDT, Spain is already in CET

Let me recalculate:
- October 25, 2026, 11:59 PM PDT = October 26, 2026 at 6:59 AM UTC
- Madrid in CET (UTC+1) = October 26, 2026 at 7:59 AM

ANSWER: 2026-10-26 07:59

I live in Lima, Peru. A contest page says: "Deadline: 12:00 noon Eastern Time on the day the US ends daylight saving time in 2026."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

I need to find when the US ends daylight saving time in 2026, then convert 12:00 noon Eastern Time to Lima, Peru time.

**When does the US end daylight saving time in 2026?**
In the US, daylight saving time ends on the first Sunday in November. In 2026, that will be November 1, 2026.

**What is the time zone difference?**
- At 12:00 noon Eastern Time on November 1, 2026, the US will have just ended DST at 2:00 AM that morning, so it will be Eastern Standard Time (EST).
- EST is UTC-5
- Lima, Peru is UTC-5 year-round (Peru does not observe daylight saving time)

**Converting the time:**
Since both EST and Lima time are UTC-5, 12:00 noon EST = 12:00 noon Lima time.

ANSWER: 2026-11-01 12:00

I live in Tokyo, Japan. A contest page says: "Deadline: December 31, 2026, 24:00 AoE."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

I need to convert December 31, 2026, 24:00 AoE to Tokyo time.

AoE stands for "Anywhere on Earth" time, which is UTC-12 (the last timezone).

24:00 AoE on December 31, 2026 is the same as 00:00 AoE on January 1, 2027.

Tokyo is in JST (Japan Standard Time), which is UTC+9.

The time difference between JST and AoE is: 9 - (-12) = 21 hours.

So when it's 00:00 January 1, 2027 in AoE, it's 21 hours later in Tokyo.
00:00 January 1, 2027 AoE + 21 hours = 21:00 January 1, 2027 JST.

ANSWER: 2027-01-01 21:00

I live in Madrid, Spain, but that week I'm traveling in New York, USA, and I need New York time. A contest page says: "The deadline is 5:00 PM Sydney time on October 5, 2026."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

I need to convert 5:00 PM Sydney time on October 5, 2026 to New York time (since you'll be in New York that week).

Let me work through the time zones:
- Sydney, Australia is in the AEDT timezone during early October (Australian Eastern Daylight Time, UTC+11)
- New York in early October 2026 will be in EDT (Eastern Daylight Time, UTC-4)

The time difference between Sydney (UTC+11) and New York (UTC-4) is 15 hours, with Sydney ahead.

So when it's 5:00 PM (17:00) on October 5 in Sydney:
- 17:00 October 5 in Sydney (UTC+11)
- Converting to UTC: 17:00 - 11 hours = 06:00 UTC on October 5
- Converting to New York (UTC-4): 06:00 - 4 hours = 02:00 on October 5

Therefore, 5:00 PM Sydney time on October 5, 2026 equals 2:00 AM New York time on October 5, 2026.

ANSWER: 2026-10-05 02:00
